summary: Iteration 49 — Decision 'Raised by' + Discussion/Comment thread. Backend pytest 10/10 PASS (test_iteration49_decision_comments.py): GET /api/decisions returns enriched created_by_name + source; GET /api/decisions/{id} returns full doc with tasks/timeline (no _id leak); POST /api/decisions/{id}/comment 200 for owner appends timeline entry kind='comment' actor/actor_id/ts, 400 for empty text, 404 for missing id, 403 for non-participant (sales user against an owner-only decision). Participant (finance as task assignee) receives notification with type='comment', entity_type='decision', entity_id=<did>. Commenter is excluded from recipients (no self-notification). Frontend Playwright — all owner flows work: (1) /?decision=<id> deep-link opens decision-dialog on approved decisions; (2) inside dialog decision-raised-by shows 'RAISED BY RAJESH SHARMA · MANUAL · 2 HRS AGO', decision-timeline renders comments (owner/actor/ts), decision-comment-input + decision-comment-send both present and functional; (3) owner posts a comment via UI → immediately appears in timeline with author + 'just now' + persists across reload/re-open; (4) status chip + dtype chip render. **CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUE FOUND**: GET /api/decisions/{id} does NOT enforce participant access — only tenant scoping. Sales user (not a participant of decision cf8147f5) receives 200 + full timeline including internal comments; only POST comment is gated at 403. The frontend renders the whole dialog (raised-by, summary, discussion thread with all comments) to sales, and only when they attempt to send does the 403 toast show. The decision-access-restricted UI panel (frontend/src/components/DecisionDialog.js:52) is unreachable because the query is never in isError state. Per PRD this GET should also 403 non-participants so the dialog shows access-restricted.

critical.issue: Does NOT enforce participant access — any tenant user can read the full decision detail (title, summary, timeline with all internal comments) even for decisions they have no involvement in. Only tenant scoping is checked (server.py:1688-1693). Per PRD, non-participants should get 403 so the frontend can show decision-access-restricted. Currently POST /comment correctly 403s but GET is a data-leak backdoor. Add: `participants = await _decision_participants(...); if user['id'] not in participants: raise HTTPException(403, ...)` mirroring the POST /comment guard.

integration_issues.issue: decision-access-restricted branch is dead code — the backend GET always returns 200 within tenant so the query never enters isError state. Once backend GET is fixed to 403 non-participants, this UI path will automatically activate.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1688-1693 GET /decisions/{id} tenant-only check is the data-leak root cause. Should mirror POST /comment's `_decision_participants` gate — or explicitly permit owner role while requiring participant membership for non-owners. Given the PRD says 'owner can access all; test the 403 primarily at the API level with sales credentials', the required behaviour is: owner bypass OR user_id in _decision_participants. Fix is 3 lines.
server.py:1696-1703 GET /decisions/{id}/timeline suffers the exact same tenant-only check — sales user can hit the timeline endpoint directly and see every comment. Same fix needed there.

DecisionDialog access-restricted branch renders a bare

heading; Radix Dialog requires a child. Wrap with Access restricted to silence the a11y console error (see console output on every dialog open).

raisedByLabel treats missing source as 'Manual'. For the seeded demo tenant every existing decision has source=null so they all display 'MANUAL' — including ones actually captured by voice. Consider backfilling `source` on process_voice_note (~server.py:710) at migration time, or hiding the segment when d.source is null.
server.py is 4544 lines — decisions block (~1650-1833) is a clean extraction candidate to routers/decisions.py alongside the analogous notification router extraction called out in iter 48.

_decision_participants includes ALL tenant owners — good, but on tenants with many owners this pushes N notifications on every comment. Consider deduping on a short window (see notif storm concern from iter 47/48).

GET /api/decisions returns full doc for every row (no _id but includes everything). This is fine now, but the list endpoint returns up to 200 decisions with tasks pre-enriched — payload could grow. Consider a leaner list projection (id, title, status, dtype, source, wa_from, created_by_name, created_at) and only fetch the full doc via /decisions/{id}.

The comment endpoint records actor+actor_id but no `edited_at` / `deleted` / `id` per comment. If any future feature needs to delete/edit comments, there's no per-entry id — timeline entries are anonymous inside a $push. Consider tagging each entry with `id: new_id()` at insert time so edit/delete-by-id becomes trivial.

rca of the issue: Root cause of the GET data-leak: when adding POST /decisions/{id}/comment (server.py:1814), the author correctly wrote _decision_participants() helper and gated POST — but forgot to apply the same gate to the pre-existing GET /decisions/{id} (line 1688) and GET /decisions/{id}/timeline (line 1696). Both still use only `{'id': decision_id, 'tenant_id': user['tenant_id']}` in the query, which lets any authenticated tenant user read the entire doc including the newly-added comment thread. Reproduction: login as sales@sharma.com (not owner, not creator, not task assignee) and GET /api/decisions/cf8147f5-2393-4f90-8713-214217bb8808 → 200 with full timeline. Verified in both curl and browser. Frontend cannot compensate because it relies on isError state which never fires. Mitigation is a 3-line fix in server.py: add `if user.get('role') != 'owner' and user['id'] not in await _decision_participants(user['tenant_id'], d): raise HTTPException(403, ...)` after the doc-fetch in both get_decision and decision_timeline.
